articles.title: Allowable Subject Matter in the Final Rejection
articles.content:
本文是探讨专利审查裁决的系列文章第三篇。根据定义，审查官的裁决至少包括部分权利要求不符合专利条件的结论。但许多裁决也指出其他权利要求可能被允许。前两篇文章分析了实体审查第一行动。Dennis Crouch，《被拒绝但有路径：首次行动中可允许的主题》，Patently-O (2026年8月17日)，以及《可允许但未全部批准：首次行动预示什么》，Patently-O (2026年8月18日)。

本文关注终裁决。我收集了2024年日历年首次终裁决的案件，并按是否识别出可允许的主题进行分类。大约21%的裁决确实指出了可允许的权利要求。

这两组案件的结果差异显著。在审查官识别出可允许权利要求的情况下，92%的申请已获授权为专利，6%被放弃。而在审查官未找到任何可允许内容的情况下，55%的申请获得专利授权，33%被放弃。
articles.summary:
by Dennis Crouch

This is the third post in a series digging into office action rejections.  As its name implies, a rejection from an examiner includes a finding that at least some claims are unpatentable. But, many rejections also indicate the allowability of other claims. The first posts looked at the first action on the merits. Dennis Crouch, Rejected, With a Road Map: Allowable Subject Matter in the First Action, Patently-O (Aug. 17, 2026), and Allowable, Not Allowed: What the First Action Predicts, Patently-O (Aug. 18, 2026).

This one moves to the final rejection. For this one I gathered cases whose first final rejection was in the calendar year 2024 and split them by whether the action identified allowable subject matter. About 21% did.

The two groups fare very differently. In cases where the examiner identified allowable claims, 92% of the applications have issued as patents and 6% have been abandoned. Where the examiner found nothing allowable, 55% have patented and 33% have been abandoned.
